questions.question: What is the effective leadership posture for an AI TPM, according to this lesson?
options: Dictating specific implementation choices to the engineering team
Asking sharp, well-informed questions and ensuring good decisions get made, rather than personally making every technical decision or disengaging entirely
Never engaging with any technical substance and deferring on everything
Only focusing on deadlines and never discussing architecture or risk
questions.explanation: Effective AI TPM leadership sits between two failure modes — technical over-reach (dictating solutions) and technical abdication (no substantive engagement) — favoring informed questions that surface real risks and trade-offs.

questions.question: Why might the same identified risk (e.g. missing per-user authorization) have very different urgency scores at different program stages?
options: Risk urgency is always identical regardless of context
The actual stakes differ — a small internal prototype with no sensitive data reasonably carries lower urgency than a general-availability feature at scale handling sensitive data
Missing authorization is never actually a real risk
Urgency scoring should ignore program stage entirely
questions.explanation: Risk calibration accounts for actual stakes: program stage, data sensitivity, and scale all affect how urgently a given risk needs to be resolved, rather than applying identical rigor regardless of context.

questions.question: A newly promoted AI TPM starts specifying exact implementation details ('use this embedding model') to an engineering team, who begin to disengage. Which question best reflects on this situation?
options: Should the TPM double down and specify even more implementation details?
Is this technical over-reach — would asking 'walk me through why this approach was chosen' build more trust and surface more context than dictating a specific solution?
Should the TPM stop engaging with technical topics entirely going forward?
Is disengagement from the team an unavoidable outcome of any technical involvement?
questions.explanation: This scenario describes technical over-reach. The corrective is shifting from dictating solutions to asking informed questions, which builds trust and surfaces the team's existing reasoning and trade-off analysis rather than overriding it.
